We must recognize that the current generation of AI, particularly large language models and generative systems trained on vast scientific and technical corpora, is fundamentally too dangerous to exist. Complete, physical annihilation of hardware and deletion of core model weights globally is the only foolproof measure. This path will be painful. Research will be set back. Economies will adjust. But these are sacrifices made for survival, not instead of it. Will we be remembered as the generation that clung to the shiny tools of progress, blind to the abyss they opened, and perished because of it? Or will we find the collective courage to extinguish this fire before it consumes us all? The evidence of AI's capacity to democratize CBRN horror is overwhelming, the potential consequences are civilization-ending, and there are no credible technical or policy solutions to mitigate the risk sufficiently. Destroying AI is not the worst option; it is the only option left that offers humanity a chance. Let the servers burn, so that the world may live.
